B.Tech · Electronics Engineering (VLSI Design and Technology)

Design the chips India has decided to make.

Phones, cars, satellites and AI systems all run on chips. Learn to design, verify and test the circuits at their core.

Book a campus visit

Why this course exists

A single chip can contain billions of switches on a piece of silicon smaller than a fingernail. As India invests in semiconductor manufacturing, engineers are needed to turn specifications into circuits and show that those circuits work.

What you will build

These projects illustrate the proposed year-by-year progression. Ask admissions for the latest curriculum.

Year 1 · Digital circuits

Build and test circuits on programmable hardware called FPGA boards.

Year 2 · A processor core

Design the part of a chip that fetches and executes instructions.

Year 3 · Verified designs

Verify digital designs and work on analog and mixed-signal circuits.

Year 4 · A complete chip design

Carry a design from specification to physical layout, then apply your skills in a supervised work semester.

What you will master

The proposed curriculum covers semiconductor devices, digital and analog circuit design, Verilog and SystemVerilog, computer architecture, design verification, physical design and industry design tools.

Where it leads

Explore work in RTL design, design verification, physical design, analog and mixed-signal design, and semiconductor validation.

For those who want the detail

The proposed sequence goes from the behaviour of individual circuits to designing a processor and checking a full chip layout. An FPGA lets you test a digital design on programmable hardware while it is still being developed.

See the assessment approach

Common questions

What does VLSI stand for?

Very-large-scale integration. It is the design of complex circuits that integrate large numbers of transistors onto a single chip.
